96586.subject: Technical Drawing
96586.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
96586.explanation: The compass is specifically designed to draw circles and arcs of different sizes by adjusting the distance between its legs. Other tools like the protractor, set square, and T-square do not serve this purpose.

96587.subject: Technical Drawing
96587.question_text: What is the dimension of an A3 drawing sheet in millimeters?
96587.explanation: The A3 sheet size is part of the ISO 216 standard and measures 297 mm × 420 mm. This is derived by halving the longer side of an A2 sheet (420 mm × 594 mm).

96588.subject: Technical Drawing
96588.question_text: Which line type is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
96588.explanation: A dashed line (also called a hidden line) is used to show edges or features that are not visible in the current view but exist in the object. Continuous thick lines represent visible outlines, while chain lines are used for center lines.

96589.subject: Technical Drawing
96589.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
96589.explanation: Bisecting an angle requires drawing arcs from the vertex and intersecting points, then connecting the vertex to the intersection. Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex is not part of the standard angle bisection procedure.

options.text: Drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect the arms of the angle
Drawing arcs from the intersection points to find a new point
Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex
Connecting the vertex to the intersection of the arcs

96590.subject: Technical Drawing
96590.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed:
96590.explanation: In first-angle projection, the front view is placed above the plan (top view) and to the left of the side view. This is the standard used in Ghana and many other countries following ISO conventions.

options.text: Above the plan and to the right of the side view
Above the plan and to the left of the side view
Below the plan and to the right of the side view
Below the plan and to the left of the side view

96591.subject: Technical Drawing
96591.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it?
96591.explanation: A half section is used for symmetrical objects to show both the exterior and interior details in a single view by removing one-quarter of the object. Full sections cut through the entire object, while revolved and removed sections are used for specific features.

96592.subject: Technical Drawing
96592.question_text: In an isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
96592.explanation: In isometric projection, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are equally spaced at 120° to each other. This creates a 3D representation where all dimensions are drawn to the same scale.

96593.subject: Technical Drawing
96593.question_text: Which of the following shapes cannot be developed into a flat surface without distortion?
96593.explanation: A sphere is a double-curved surface and cannot be developed into a flat plane without distortion. Prisms, pyramids, and cylinders can be unfolded into flat patterns (developments).

96594.subject: Technical Drawing
96594.question_text: Which of the following is a correct dimensioning practice?
96594.explanation: Dimensions should be placed outside the outline of the object to avoid cluttering the drawing. They should not be duplicated, and extension lines should not cross dimension lines unless necessary.

options.text: Placing dimensions inside the outline of the object
Placing dimensions outside the outline of the object
Repeating the same dimension in multiple views
Crossing extension lines with dimension lines

96595.subject: Technical Drawing
96595.question_text: Which of the following fasteners is used to prevent relative motion between two parts by friction?
96595.explanation: A set screw is a type of fastener used to secure an object within or against another object, typically by friction. Bolts, rivets, and keys serve different purposes in mechanical assemblies.

84062.subject: Technical Drawing
84062.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
84062.explanation: The compass is a drawing instrument used to draw circles and arcs of different sizes. It consists of two legs, one with a pointed end and the other with a pencil or pen attachment.

84063.subject: Technical Drawing
84063.question_text: What is the size of an A2 drawing sheet in millimeters?
84063.explanation: The standard size of an A2 drawing sheet is 420 mm × 594 mm, following the ISO 216 standard for paper sizes.

84064.subject: Technical Drawing
84064.question_text: Which type of line is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
84064.explanation: A dashed line (or hidden line) is used to represent edges and details that are not visible in the current view of an orthographic projection.

84065.subject: Technical Drawing
84065.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
84065.explanation: Drawing a line parallel to one of the arms of the angle is not a step in bisecting an angle. The correct steps involve drawing arcs from the vertex and intersecting points to locate the bisector.

options.text: Draw an arc from the vertex intersecting both arms of the angle
Draw arcs from the points of intersection to locate the bisector
Draw a line parallel to one of the arms of the angle
Join the vertex to the intersection of the arcs to form the bisector

84066.subject: Technical Drawing
84066.question_text: What is the interior angle of a regular hexagon?
84066.explanation:
The interior angle of a regular hexagon can be calculated using the formula:
$ ext{Interior angle} = rac{(n-2) imes 180°}{n}$
where $n = 6$.
Thus, $ rac{(6-2) imes 180°}{6} = 120°$.

84067.subject: Technical Drawing
84067.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed:
84067.explanation: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed above the top view, and the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view.

options.text: To the right of the side view
To the left of the side view

84068.subject: Technical Drawing
84068.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it?
84068.explanation: A half section is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it, leaving the other half intact for external details.

84069.subject: Technical Drawing
84069.question_text: In isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
84069.explanation: In isometric drawing, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are inclined at 120° to each other to represent a 3D object on a 2D plane.

84070.subject: Technical Drawing
84070.question_text: Which of the following is not a principle of dimensioning in technical drawing?
84070.explanation: Dimensions should not be duplicated in different views. Each dimension should be placed in the view where it is most clearly represented.

options.text: Dimensions should be placed outside the views where possible
Dimensions should be duplicated in different views
Dimension lines should not cross each other
Leader lines should be used for notes and specifications

84071.subject: Technical Drawing
84071.question_text: Which of the following is not typically included in a working drawing?
84071.explanation: A perspective sketch is not typically included in a working drawing. Working drawings usually consist of orthographic projections, dimensions, notes, and specifications.

85545.subject: Technical Drawing
85545.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw horizontal lines?
85545.explanation: The T-square is a drawing tool specifically designed to draw horizontal lines. It is used in conjunction with a drawing board to ensure accuracy.

85546.subject: Technical Drawing
85546.question_text: What is the size of an A2 drawing sheet in millimeters?
85546.explanation: The standard size of an A2 drawing sheet is 420 mm × 594 mm, following the ISO 216 standard for paper sizes.

85547.subject: Technical Drawing
85547.question_text: Which line type is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
85547.explanation: A dashed line (short dashes) is used to represent hidden details in orthographic projections, indicating edges or features not visible in the current view.

85548.subject: Technical Drawing
85548.question_text: What is the recommended height for uppercase letters in technical drawings?
85548.explanation: The recommended height for uppercase letters in technical drawings is 3.5 mm to 5 mm, depending on the sheet size and clarity requirements.

85549.subject: Technical Drawing
85549.question_text: Which of the following constructions is used to bisect a given angle?
85549.explanation: The angle bisector construction involves drawing arcs from the angle's vertex and intersecting points to divide the angle into two equal parts.

85550.subject: Technical Drawing
85550.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, where is the front view located relative to the plan?
85550.explanation: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is located above the plan, following the convention where the object is imagined to be in the first quadrant.

options.text: To the right of the plan
To the left of the plan

85551.subject: Technical Drawing
85551.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting it halfway?
85551.explanation: A half section is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting it halfway, revealing both external and internal features in a single view.

85552.subject: Technical Drawing
85552.question_text: What is the angle between the isometric axes in an isometric drawing?
85552.explanation: In an isometric drawing, the angle between the isometric axes is 120°, creating a three-dimensional representation with equal foreshortening along each axis.

85553.subject: Technical Drawing
85553.question_text: Which of the following is a correct dimensioning practice?
85553.explanation: In dimensioning, dimensions should not be duplicated to avoid confusion and ensure clarity in the drawing. Each dimension should appear only once.

85554.subject: Technical Drawing
85554.question_text: What does a scale of 1:50 represent in a technical drawing?
85554.explanation: A scale of 1:50 means that 1 unit on the drawing represents 50 units on the actual object, commonly used for architectural and engineering drawings.

options.text: 1 unit on the drawing equals 1 unit on the object
1 unit on the drawing equals 50 units on the object
50 units on the drawing equals 1 unit on the object
The drawing is 50 times larger than the object

60054.subject: Technical Drawing
60054.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
60054.explanation: The compass is a drawing instrument used to draw circles and arcs of different sizes. It consists of two legs, one with a pointed end and the other with a pencil or pen attachment.

60055.subject: Technical Drawing
60055.question_text: What is the size of an A2 drawing sheet in millimeters?
60055.explanation: The A2 sheet size is part of the ISO 216 standard, measuring 420 mm × 594 mm. Each A-series sheet is half the area of the previous size when folded along its longer side.

60056.subject: Technical Drawing
60056.question_text: Which line type is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
60056.explanation: A dashed line (also called a hidden line) is used to show edges or features that are not visible in the current view but exist in the object.

60057.subject: Technical Drawing
60057.question_text: What is the recommended height for capital letters in technical drawings according to WAEC standards?
60057.explanation: The standard height for capital letters in technical drawings is 3.5 mm, ensuring clarity and uniformity in engineering and architectural documents.

60058.subject: Technical Drawing
60058.question_text: Which of the following constructions is used to bisect a given angle?
60058.explanation: To bisect an angle, an arc is drawn from the vertex, intersecting the arms of the angle. From these intersection points, further arcs are drawn to locate the bisector.

options.text: Drawing arcs from the vertex and intersecting points
Using a protractor to measure half the angle
Drawing a tangent to the angle arms

60059.subject: Technical Drawing
60059.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, where is the front view located relative to the plan?
60059.explanation: In first-angle projection, the front view is placed above the plan, while the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view.

options.text: To the right of the plan
To the left of the plan

60060.subject: Technical Drawing
60060.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it?
60060.explanation: A half section is used to display the internal features of a symmetrical object by removing one-quarter of it, allowing both external and internal details to be shown in a single view.

60061.subject: Technical Drawing
60061.question_text: What is the angle between the isometric axes in an isometric drawing?
60061.explanation: In isometric projection, the three axes (length, width, and height) are equally spaced at 120° to each other, creating a 3D representation on a 2D plane.

60062.subject: Technical Drawing
60062.question_text: Which of the following is a correct dimensioning practice in technical drawings?
60062.explanation: Dimensions should be placed outside the outline of the object unless clarity requires otherwise. This prevents clutter and ensures readability.

options.text: Placing dimensions inside the object outline
Placing dimensions outside the object outline
Using only one arrowhead for each dimension

60063.subject: Technical Drawing
60063.question_text: What does a scale of 1:50 represent in a technical drawing?
60063.explanation: A scale of 1:50 means that 1 unit on the drawing represents 50 units on the actual object. This is a reducing scale used for large objects.

options.text: 1 unit on the drawing equals 5 units on the object
1 unit on the drawing equals 50 units on the object
50 units on the drawing equal 1 unit on the object
The drawing is 50 times larger than the object
